thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Pushes Mostly Higher as S&P, Nasdaq Halt Four-Day Skids

title: Close Update: Wall Street Pushes Mostly Higher as S&P, Nasdaq Halt Four-Day Skids
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Pushes Mostly Higher as S&P, Nasdaq Halt Four-Day Skids September 10, 2018, 04:20:22 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Equities in the U.S. were mostly higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite halting four-day losing streaks as optimism about more tax cuts helped overshadow a downbeat day for tech giant Apple ( AAPL ).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was unable to join its peers in the win column with Apple's loss weighing after the company came into the sights of President Donald Trump's tweeting over the weekend and Travelers Cos. ( TRV ) weakened as Atlantic coast states prepared for a category four Hurricane Florence.
Markets were dented last week as Trump jolted sentiment with talk of tariffs on China and a better-than-expected jobs report raised worries about faster interest-rate increases. But reports Monday that US House Republicans are poised to introduce another round of tax cuts this week helped turn equity sentiment to the upside.
Among the S&P's sectors, information technology rose 0.3% as semiconductors recovered some of their recent losses. Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) led the way on the S&P, rising 9.2% as Susquehanna said the company is gaining share in three key markets.
Utilities rose 0.6% in the best performance among the S&P's groups, while telecoms, real estate and industrials were also among the gainers. On the downside, health care retreated 0.3% and financials dipped 0.1% as insurers weakened ahead of the storm.
Nike ( NKE ) rose the most among the blue-chips on the Dow after Wedbush added $5 to its price target on the athletics retailer, setting it at $90 ahead of fiscal first-quarter results due in about two weeks. Home Depot ( HD ) was also in the green, as was Lowe's (LOW) with Florence expected to hit land later in the week. But the Dow faltered overall as UnitedHealth Group (UNH) and Boeing (BA) dropped.
